newsitem.title: USA: Pimco to acquire certain Oppenheimer interests for $265 million.
newsitem.headline: Pimco to acquire certain Oppenheimer interests for $265 million.

text.p: Pimco Advisors LP and its affiliate Thomson Advisory Group Inc. will buy interests from Oppenheimer Group Inc. for about $265 million in preferred stock and assumed debt, the companies said Friday.
With $110 billion in assets managed by Pimco Advisors and $48 billion managed by Oppenheimer Capital, the deal will create one of the nation's largest investment management firms, they said.
The acquisition is expected to diversify PImco's product lines and distribution channels.

Under the definitive agreement, Pimco and Thomson will acquire a one-third, managing general partner interest in Oppenheimer Capital and the 1 percent general partner interest in Oppenheimer Capital LP. They will also take over all of the stock of Advantage Advisers, an affiliate of Oppenheimer Group that manages eight closed-end funds, they said.
Oppenheimer Capital will function as an indirect subsidiary of Pimco, with its current employees and structure.

The transaction covers only the private interests Oppenheimer Group holds in Oppenheimer Capital and Oppenheimer Capital L.P. and not the publicly traded units of Oppenheimer Capital, L.P., they said.
To facilitate the acquisition, Oppenheimer Group will spin off all of its stock in its Oppenheimer Financial Corp. subsidiary, which will own the brokerage business of Oppenheimer & Co. Inc.

TAG Inc., a limited partner of Pimco, will then issue about $233 million of convertible, preferred stock to the shareholders of Oppenheimer Group and will assume about $32 million in debt in exchange for the two general partner interests and the stock of Advantage Advisers.

After the exchange, TAG will contribute the general partner interest in Oppenheimer Capital to Pimco, which will issue about $233 million of new Class A Limited Partner units, at $25.50 a unit, to TAG.
Pimco's stock rose 12.5 cents to $25.625, while Oppenheimer edged down 37.5 cents to $37.625 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
